title: Restart Days Worksheet for Resumed Payment Arrangements
content:
When a suspended plan under Payment Arrangements resumes, its restart days fix when the first installment after resumption falls due.

## Definition

The restart days are the calendar days from the resumption date, the handling date, to the due date of the first installment after resumption.

The earliest restart day is the restart clock offset plus the restart lead plus the returned-debit cool-down plus the statement lead, counted in calendar days from the handling date, and the restart days are the earliest restart day placed on the plan's schedule by the restart alignment, never fewer than the type's resume minimum before the next installment.

The restart clock offset is zero, so the clock starts on the handling date; the restart lead is the type's resume minimum before the next installment; the returned-debit cool-down and the statement lead are 0 days; and the restart days are the earliest restart day itself.

## Assembly

| Element | Value |
|---|---|
| Restart clock offset | 0 days (the clock starts on the handling date) |
| Restart lead | The arrangement type's resume minimum, a product figure of the type |
| Returned-debit cool-down | 0 days |
| Statement lead | 0 days |
| Earliest restart day | The total of the four elements above, in calendar days from the handling date |
| Placement on the schedule | The earliest restart day itself |
| Floor | Never fewer than the type's resume minimum |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A plan of a type whose resume minimum reads 14 days in this illustration resumes on a handling date of 3 August.

- Earliest restart day: 0 plus 14 plus 0 plus 0 is 14 days.
- Placement: 14 days.
- Floor: 14 is not fewer than 14, so the restart days are 14.
- The first installment after resumption falls due 14 calendar days after 3 August, on 17 August.
